card: Documents in the bitcoinkernel C API header that the btck_WriteBytes callback may receive a null pointer when the size argument is zero. Without this specification, downstream foreign language bindings implementing custom serialization writers can experience undefined behavior if their language requires non-null pointers for zero-length slices. The author notes that internal vector-backed callers directly forward std::vector::data(), which yields null for empty script and witness elements.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete patch, confirming a 4-line documentation comment addition to btck_WriteBytes in src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h.
evidence: "The header does not say whether the bytes pointer can be null when size is zero. It can: `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` passes `std::vector::data()` straight through, and that may be null for an empty element." (PR description)
"This matters for bindings rather than for C callers." (Commit 76359bee61)
problem: The bitcoinkernel C API documentation does not state whether the bytes pointer can be null when size is zero. Because internal implementations pass through std::vector::data() directly—which can be null for empty elements such as empty witness stack items—foreign language bindings that require non-null pointers for zero-length slices risk undefined behavior or crashes.

risk.why: This is a documentation-only addition to a header comment that does not modify any executable code.

summary: Document in the libbitcoinkernel C API header that the buffer pointer passed to the btck_WriteBytes callback can be null when size is zero. It warns binding authors that constructing a language-level slice or array view may require handling null pointers.
